rows.speaker: الحسن وجعفر بن محمد
rows.claim: They say the treasure was a gold tablet inscribed with counsel about destiny, provision, death, judgment, worldly change, and the testimony of faith.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن وجعفر بن محمد: «كان لوحا من ذهب مكتوبا فيه:

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Some reports raise a further inscription to the Prophet, beginning with counsel to the worried; the quoted wording is fragmentary in this text.
rows.anchor: وقد روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم هذا القول مرفوعا في بعض الروايات أنه كان مكتوبا في ذلك اللوح

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says the treasure was simply money.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة كان ذلك الكنز مالا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report from Abu al-Darda attributes to the Prophet that the treasure consisted of gold and silver.
rows.anchor: مكحول عن [أبي] الدرداء قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله: وكان تحته كنز لهما، قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The boys' father was the pious Kashih; their protection is attributed to his righteousness although no righteousness of the boys is mentioned, and seven generations separated them from him; he was a traveler.
rows.anchor: وكان أبوهما صالحا، واسمه كاشح، وكان من الأتقياء.

rows.speaker: محمد بن المنكدر
rows.claim: God preserves a righteous person's children, grandchildren, clan, and nearby homes in divine protection and covering.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن المنكدر قال: إن الله عز وجل ليحفظ بالرجل الصالح ولده وولد ولده، وعشيرته التي هو فيها،

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: When seeing his son, Saeed would increase his prayers hoping that his own worship would bring the boy protection, and he recited this verse.
rows.anchor: وعن سعيد بن المسيب أنه كان إذا رأى ابنه قال: أي بني لأزيدن صلاتي من أجلك،

rows.speaker: يحيى بن إسماعيل بن مسلمة بن كهيل
rows.claim: He recounts that his older sister lost her reason for many years and lived apart, yet remained devoted to prayer and ritual purity.
rows.anchor: قال: كانت لي أخت أسن مني فاختلطت وذهب عقلها، وتوحشت، وكانت في غرفة

rows.speaker: يحيى بن إسماعيل بن مسلمة بن كهيل
rows.claim: In a dream the sister was told God protected her father through her grandfather and her through her father; she chose patient endurance and Paradise, then received both healing and the reward.
rows.anchor: فقيل: إن الله قد حفظ أباك إسماعيل بن سلمة بن كهيل بسلمة جدك، وحفظك بأبيك إسماعيل،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The boys would reach their full strength and power; one view sets maturity at eighteen years.
rows.anchor: فأراد ربك يا موسى أن يبلغا أشدهما، أي يدركا شدتهما وقوتهما. وقيل: ثماني عشرة سنة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The boys would recover the treasure stored beneath the wall when they matured.
rows.anchor: ويستخرجا كنزهما المكنوز تحت الجدار،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker says he acted by God's command, not by personal judgment or initiative.
rows.anchor: وما فعلته عن أمري برأيي ومن تلقاء نفسي، بل فعلت عن أمر الله عز وجل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final explanation is the interpretation Moses could not patiently bear; asṭāʿ and istaṭāʿ have the same meaning.
rows.anchor: ذلك تأويل ما لم تسطع عليه صبرا و (اسطاع) و (استطاع) بمعنى واحد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Authorities disagree whether Dhu al-Qarnayn was a prophet or a just, righteous king; the passage leaves both views open.
rows.anchor: كان نبيا. وقال الآخرون: كان ملكا عادلا صالحا.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid counts four rulers of the earth: the believers Solomon and Dhu al-Qarnayn, and the unbelievers Nimrod and Bukhtnassar.
rows.anchor: قال: سمعت مجاهدا يقول: ملك الأرض أربعة: مؤمنان، وكافران.

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One explanation says he was called Dhu al-Qarnayn because he ruled Rome and Persia.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا في سبب تسميته بذي القرنين، فقال بعضهم: سمي بذلك، لأنه ملك الروم وفارس.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation derives the name from something resembling two horns on his head.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لأنه كان في رأسه شبه القرنين.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A dream of grasping the sun by its two horns was interpreted to mean that he would travel east and west.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لأنه رأى في منامه كأنه أخذ بقرني الشمس فكان تأويل رؤياه أنه طاف الشرق والغرب.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account says people struck his right horn and then his left when he called them to monotheism.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لأنه دعا قومه إلى التوحيد فضربوه على قرنه الأيمن ثم دعاهم إلى التوحيد فضربوه على قرنه الأيسر.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view connects his name to his two beautiful locks, since a lock of hair can be called a horn.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لأنه كان له ذؤابتان حسناوان، والذؤابة تسمى قرنا.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says he was noble on both sides, from a distinguished family through both parents.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لأنه كريم الطرفين من أهل بيت شرف من قبل أبيه وأمه.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some say two generations of people died out during his lifetime.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لأنه انقرض في وقته قرنان من الناس، وهو حي.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says he fought with both his hand and his stirrup.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لأنه إذا كان حارب قاتل بيده وركابه جميعا.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some say he was granted knowledge of both the outward and inward realms.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لأنه أعطي علم الظاهر الباطن.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A final explanation says he entered both light and darkness.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لأنه دخل النور والظلمة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God established Dhu al-Qarnayn on earth by settling him as its ruler and guiding him along its routes.
rows.anchor: إنا مكنا له في الأرض أوطأنا له في الأرض فملكها وهديناه طرقها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave him the means for everything people need; another interpretation makes these the knowledge and means rulers use to conquer cities and fight enemies.
rows.anchor: وآتيناه من كل شيء يحتاج إليه الخلق. وقيل: من كل شيء يستعين به الملوك على فتح المدن

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan interprets the means as a passage that took Dhu al-Qarnayn wherever he wished.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: بلاغا إلى حيث أراد.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says God brought the earth's regions near to him, as He subjected the wind to Solomon.
rows.anchor: وقيل: قربنا إليه أقطار الأرض، كما سخرنا الريح لسليمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb atbāʿa means that he took and traveled along a route.
rows.anchor: فأتبع: سلك وسار.

rows.speaker: قراء أهل الكوفة
rows.claim: The Kufans read the verb with a hamza cut, including in the later occurrence, with the second verb jussive, meaning he reached a route.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أهل الكوفة: (فأتبع) ... ، (ثم أتبع) بقطع الألف وجزم الثاني: لحق سببا،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses sabab as a stopping place.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: منزلا،

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses sabab as a road between east and west, comparing it to the paths named in 40:36.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: طريقا بين المشرق والمغرب، نظير قوله تعالى: لعلي أبلغ الأسباب أسباب السماوات

rows.speaker: قراء العبادلة والحسن وأبو جعفر وابن عامر وأيوب وأهل الكوفة
rows.claim: These readers recite ḥāmiyah with a long alif, meaning hot; a report from Abu Dharr likewise has the Prophet say the sun sets in a hot spring.
rows.anchor: قرأ العبادلة: عبد الله بن مسعود وعبد الله بن عمر وعبد الله بن عمرو

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: In a report from Abu Dharr, the Prophet answers that the sun sets in a hot spring.
rows.anchor: عن أبي ذر قال: كنت ردف النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: «يا أبا ذر أين تغرب هذه؟»

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: He reports the Prophet describing sunset as entering God's fiercely hot fire, which would burn the earth if not restrained by God's command.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن عمرو: نظر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى الشمس حين غابت فقال: «في نار الله الحامية، في نار الله الحامية

rows.speaker: قراء الباقون
rows.claim: The other readers recite ḥamʾah, with hamza and no alif, meaning a spring of black mud.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: حمئة مهموزة بغير ألف، يعني: ذات حمأة، وهي الطينة السوداء.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Ubayy ibn Kaʿb taught him the reading ḥamʾah as the Messenger of God had taught Ubayy.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: أقرأنيها أبي بن كعب كما أقرأه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: تغرب في عين حمئة

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb says the Torah describes the sun setting in a black spring, agreeing with Ibn Abbas's reading.
rows.anchor: وقال كعب: أجدها في التوراة: (في عين سوداء) ، فوافق ابن عباس.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In a discussion before Muawiya, Ibn Abbas objects to ḥāmiyah in favor of ḥamʾah; Ibn Umar agrees with Muawiya's reading, and Ibn Abbas says the Quran was revealed in his house.
rows.anchor: (وجدها تغرب في عين حامية) فقلت: ما نقرؤها إلا حمئة. فقال معاوية لعبد الله بن عمر:

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Asked where the sun sets in the Torah, Kaʿb answers that he finds it setting in water and mud.
rows.anchor: قال: أما العربية فأنتم أعلم بها، وأما الشمس فإني أجدها في التوراة تغرب في ماء وطين.

rows.speaker: تبع
rows.claim: A poem attributed to Tubbaʿ describes the setting sun in a dark mud spring; Ibn Abbas records the verse as support for ḥamʾah.
rows.anchor: قلت: قول تبع: قد كان ذو القرنين قبلي مسلما … ملكا تدين له الملوك وتسجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poem's terms are glossed: khalb means mud in their speech, thaʾṭ means mud, and ḥarmad means black.
rows.anchor: قال: فقال ابن عباس: ما الخلب؟ قلت: الطين بكلامهم. قال: فما الثأط؟ قلت:

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliya says he heard that the sun is in a spring and the spring casts it toward the east.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: بلغني أن الشمس في عين، تقذفها العين إلى المشرق.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people at the spring are offered either punishment by killing if they refuse Islam or kindness through pardon; another gloss is capture followed by teaching guidance.
rows.anchor: إما أن تعذب: إما أن تقتلهم إن لم يدخلوا في الإسلام وإما أن تتخذ فيهم حسنا، أي تعفو وتصفح.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who wronged are disbelievers; Dhu al-Qarnayn would kill them, then they would return to God for a severe, dreadful punishment in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: قال أما من ظلم، أي كفر فسوف نعذبه: نقتله ثم يرد إلى ربه في الآخرة

rows.speaker: قراء أهل الكوفة
rows.claim: The Kufans read jazāʾ in the accusative with nunation, treating it as a verbal noun: the people receive the good as recompense.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة جزاء نصبا منونا على معنى: فله الحسنى جزاء نصب على المصدر،

rows.speaker: قراء الباقون
rows.claim: Other readers use the nominative in an annexation construction; al-ḥusnā can mean righteous deeds or Paradise, either of which is the object of the recompense.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بالرفع على الإضافة. ولها وجهان: أحدهما أن يكون المراد بالحسنى: الأعمال الصالحة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhu al-Qarnayn would speak gently and make matters easy for the believer; Mujahid glosses yusr as what is good and recognized.
rows.anchor: وسنقول له من أمرنا يسرا أي نلين له القول، ونهون له الأمر.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the people had no shelter from the sun because no building could remain there; they stayed in a watering place until sunset, then went to their work and fields.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: لم يكن بينهم وبين الشمس ستر وذلك أنهم كانوا في مكان لا يستقر عليهم بناء،

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says their land could not bear buildings; when the sun rose they plunged into water, then emerged and grazed like animals as it climbed.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: كانت أرضهم أرضا لا تحتمل البناء، وكانوا إذا طلعت عليهم الشمس تهوروا في الماء،

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj tells of an army warned to leave before sunrise; it waited, saw corpses of earlier troops killed by the sun, and fled across the earth.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: جاءهم جيش مرة فقال لهم أهلها: لا تطلع عليكم الشمس وأنتم بها،

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada reports the identification that these people were the Zanj.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: ويقال: إنهم الزنج.

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi identifies them as Tarīs, Taʾwīl, and Mansak, naked, barefoot, and blind to truth.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: هم تاريس وتاويل ومنسك عراة حفاة عماة عن الحق،

rows.speaker: عمرو بن مالك بن أمية
rows.claim: A traveler account says a people beyond China lived near the sea, slept on one ear, saw the sun rise over water like oil, and caught fish that cooked in its heat.
rows.anchor: فإذا أحدهم يفرش أذنه ويلبس الأخرى قال: وكان صاحبي يحسن لسانهم فسألهم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One interpretation of ka-dhālika is that Dhu al-Qarnayn reached sunrise just as he had reached sunset.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: كذلك اختلفوا فيه، فقال بعضهم: يعني كما بلغ مغرب الشمس فكذلك بلغ مطلعها.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation says he followed a route there just as he had followed a route before.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أتبع سببا كما أتبع سببا.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A third interpretation compares the peoples and judgments at sunrise with those he encountered and judged at sunset.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كما وجد [القبيلتين] عند مغرب الشمس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The comparison continues: he found and judged the people at sunrise by the same rule he used for the earlier people.
rows.anchor: وحكم فيهم، كذلك وجد عند مطلع الشمس فحكم فيهم بحكم أولئك.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reading takes ka-dhālika as introducing the state and account of the peoples as God related it; God knew all Dhu al-Qarnayn possessed and controlled.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن الله عز وجل لما قص عليه خبره قال: كذلك أي كذلك أمرهم والخبر عنهم كما قصصنا عليك،

rows.speaker: قراء ابن كثير وأبي عمرو وعاصم
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Asim read al-saddayn with an open sīn; the others use a damma, and al-Kisai regards both as dialects for the two mountains Dhu al-Qarnayn blocked.
rows.anchor: حتى إذا بلغ بين السدين بفتح السين، ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وعاصم. الباقون بالضم. قال الكسائي: هما لغتان،

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima distinguishes a human-made barrier, sadd with an open sīn, from al-sudd with a damma, made by God.
rows.anchor: قال عكرمة: ما كان صنعة بني آدم فهو سد- بفتح السين- وما كان من صنع الله عز وجل فهو السد، بالضم.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the two barriers as Armenia and Azerbaijan.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: السدان أرمينية وآذربيجان.

rows.speaker: قراء الأعمش ويحيى بن وثاب وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: These readers pronounce yufqihūn with passive-like yā and a kasra on qāf, meaning they scarcely understand or make others understand speech.
rows.anchor: قرأ الأعمش ويحيى بن وثاب وحمزة والكسائي يفقهون بضم الياء، وكسر القاف

rows.speaker: قراء الباقون
rows.claim: The other readers use open yā and qāf, meaning they understand and comprehend speech.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: يفقهون بفتح الياء والقاف، أي ويعلمون ويفقهون قولا.

rows.speaker: قراء ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud's reading adds that another people spoke to Dhu al-Qarnayn on their behalf, explaining the mediation between them.
rows.anchor: في قراءة ابن مسعود: (لا يكادون يفقهون قولا، قال الذين من دونهم يا ذا القرنين)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further gloss says the people could scarcely distinguish good from evil or guidance from error.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه: لا يكادون يفقهون خيرا من شر، ولا ضلالا من هدى،

rows.speaker: قراء عاصم والأعرج
rows.claim: Asim and al-Araj pronounce Yaʾjūj and Maʾjūj with hamza; the others omit it, and both are accepted dialects.
rows.anchor: إن يأجوج ومأجوج قرأهما عاصم والأعرج مهموزين، الباقون بغير همزة. وهما لغتان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their names are said to derive from the blaze and sparks of fire, likening their great numbers and ferocity to it.
rows.anchor: قالوا: وأصله من (أجيج النار) ، وهو ضوؤها وشررها، شبهوا به في كثرتهم وشدتهم.

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه ومقاتل بن سليمان
rows.claim: Wahb and Muqatil say Gog and Magog descend from Japheth, son of Noah.
rows.anchor: قال وهب بن منبه ومقاتل بن سليمان: هو من ولد يافث ابن نوح،

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak calls them a people from the Turks.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: هم جيل من الترك.

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb gives an unusual origin account: they descend from Adam alone, without Eve, after Adam's emission mixed into soil.
rows.anchor: وقال كعب: هم نادرة من ولد آدم من غير حواء،

rows.speaker: سعيد بن عبد العزيز
rows.claim: Saeed ibn Abd al-Aziz says their corruption consists of eating people.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن عبد العزيز: فسادهم في الأرض أنهم كانوا يأكلون الناس.

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says they emerge in spring, consume everything green and carry away everything dry, causing severe harm and killing people.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: كانوا يخرجون إلى أرضهم أيام الربيع فلا يدعون فيها شيئا أخضر إلا أكلوه،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation takes the corruption to mean the devastation they will cause when they emerge.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه: أنهم سيفسدون في الأرض عند خروجهم.

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Masud says each of Gog and Magog comprises four hundred thousand peoples, and a man lives until a thousand armed male descendants are born to him.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله قال: سألت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن يأجوج ومأجوج، فقال: «يأجوج أمة ومأجوج أمة، كل أمة أربعمائة ألف أمة،

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The report describes three types: cedar-like figures 120 cubits tall, figures 120 cubits in both height and width, and people who use one ear as bedding and the other as a cover; they eat animals and the dead, and are placed from Syria to Khurasan and drink eastern rivers and Lake Tiberias.
rows.anchor: قال: «هم ثلاثة أصناف: صنف منهم أمثال الأرز» قيل: يا رسول الله، وما الأرز؟ قال: «شجرة بالشام

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb says Dhu al-Qarnayn was a Roman, the only son of an elderly woman, named Alexander, and became a righteous servant; God commissioned him among all earth's peoples and equipped him with extraordinary understanding, strength, and the armies of light and darkness.
rows.anchor: قال وهب بن منبه: كان ذو القرنين رجلا من الروم، ابن عجوز من عجائزهم ليس لها ولد غيره،

rows.speaker: ذو القرنين
rows.claim: In Wahb's account, Dhu al-Qarnayn asks how he can address, understand, judge, and govern the many peoples, lacking every required ability and force.
rows.anchor: قال ذو القرنين. «يا إلهي إنك قد ندبتني لأمر عظيم لا يقدر قدره إلا أنت،

rows.speaker: الله تعالى
rows.claim: God promises to grant him comprehension, speech, hearing, sight, memory, strength, courage, authority, and light and darkness as obedient armies.
rows.anchor: قال الله تعالى: «إني سأطوقك ما حملتك: أشرح لك صدرك فتسمع كل شيء،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Wahb's narrative, Dhu al-Qarnayn surrounds the western peoples in darkness, calls them to worship God, gathers converts into an army, and subdues those who refuse before they join his call.
rows.anchor: فلما رأى ذلك كابرهم بالظلمة، فضرب حولهم ثلاثة عساكر منها فأحاط بهم في كل مكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He travels toward the right side of the earth with darkness guarding behind and light guiding ahead; God makes his plans unfailing.
rows.anchor: ثم انطلق بهم يقودهم والظلمة تسوقهم وتحرسهم من خلفهم، والنور أمامهم يقودهم ويدله،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For waterways he builds small-board boats, transports all his people, then dismantles them and gives each traveler a board to carry.
rows.anchor: فإذا انتهى إلى بحر أو مخاصة بنى سفنا من ألواح صغار أمثال البغال،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recruiting the people of Nasik and Hāwil, he reaches Mansek at sunrise and recruits its people in the same way.
rows.anchor: حتى انتهى إلى منسك عند مطلع الشمس فعمل فيها وجند منها جنودا كفعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He then turns to the left side of earth for Tawil, opposite Hāwil across the earth, and recruits its people as before.
rows.anchor: ثم كر مقبلا حتى أخذ ناحية الأرض اليسرى وهو يريد تاويل- وهي الأمة التي بحيال هاويل،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A righteous people tell Dhu al-Qarnayn that monstrous neighboring peoples eat plants, animals, insects, and people, reproduce extraordinarily fast, and may overrun and corrupt the earth; they offer payment for a barrier.
rows.anchor: قالت له أمة صالحة من الإنس: يا ذا القرنين إن بين هذين الجبلين خلقا من خلق الله تعالى

rows.speaker: ذو القرنين
rows.claim: He declines their fee because God's provision is better, asks for their help, and requests stone, iron, and copper so he can inspect the land and measure the mountains.
rows.anchor: قال ما مكني فيه ربي خير فأعينوني بقوة أجعل بينكم وبينهم ردما: أعدوا لي الصخور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative depicts the Gog and Magog people as uniform in size, male and female, each about half the height of an average man.
rows.anchor: فوجدهم على مقدار واحد، ذكرهم وأنثاهم، يبلغ طول الواحد منهم مثل نصف الرجل المربوع منا.

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali describes great variation in stature, claws, predatory teeth, abundant body hair, and huge ears used as bedding and seasonal clothing; each knows his lifespan and produces a thousand offspring before death.
rows.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طالب: «منهم من طوله شبر ومنهم من هو مفرط في الطول، لهم مخالب

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali says they obtain seasonal food in spring, consume a yearly portion until the next year, call like pigeons and wolves, and mate like animals.
rows.anchor: وهم يرزقون السينان أيام الربيع كما يستمطر الغيث لحينه فيقذفون منه كل سنة واحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountain gap lies at the eastern edge of Turk lands and spans one hundred farsakhs; Dhu al-Qarnayn digs a fifty-farsakh-wide foundation down to water, fills it with stone and molten copper, then raises iron and copper layers into a marbled wall.
rows.anchor: وهو في منقطع أرض الترك مما يلي مشرق الشمس فوجد بعد ما بينهما مائة فرسخ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After finishing the barrier, he reaches a just, equitable people marked by unity, mercy, equal treatment, and straight conduct, without rulers, judges, rich, kings, nobles, poverty, strife, violence, or illness.
rows.anchor: فوجد أمة مقسطة مقتصدة يقيمون بالسوية، ويحكمون بالعدل ويتراحمون، حالتهم واحدة وكلمتهم واحدة،

rows.speaker: القوم
rows.claim: They keep graves at their doors to remember death and leave homes without doors because no one among them is suspected and everyone is trustworthy.
rows.anchor: قالوا: عمدا فعلنا ذلك، لئلا ننسى الموت، ولا يخرج ذكره من قلوبنا.

rows.speaker: القوم
rows.claim: They need no ruler because they have no need of one, and no judges because they do not quarrel.
rows.anchor: قال: «فما بالكم ليس عليكم أمير؟» . قالوا: لا حاجة لنا إلى ذلك.

rows.speaker: القوم
rows.claim: They have no wealthy people because they do not compete to accumulate wealth.
rows.anchor: قال: «فما بالكم ليس فيكم أغنياء؟» . قالوا: لا نتكاثر.

rows.speaker: القوم
rows.claim: They have no kings because they do not boast; their hearts and relations are harmonious, so they neither quarrel nor differ.
rows.anchor: قال: «فما بالكم ليس فيكم ملوك؟» . قالوا: لا نفتخر.

rows.speaker: القوم
rows.claim: They do not fight because they occupy themselves with maturity and reflection rather than conflict.
rows.anchor: قال: «فما بالكم لا تقتتلون؟» . قالوا: من أجل أنا شبنا أنفسنا بالأحلام .

rows.speaker: القوم
rows.claim: They avoid rivalry and deceit and do not assassinate one another; the following answer says their sound hearts are free of rancor and envy.
rows.anchor: تكم واحدة، وطريقتكم مستقيمة؟» . قالوا: من قبل أنا لا نتكاثر، ولا نتخادع،

rows.speaker: القوم
rows.claim: They have no poor because they divide resources equally, and no harsh people because they practice humility.
rows.anchor: قال: «فما بالكم ليس فيكم مسكين ولا فقير؟» . قالوا: من أجل أنا نقسم بالسوية.

rows.speaker: القوم
rows.claim: They live long by pursuing truth and justice; they do not laugh because they never neglect seeking forgiveness.
rows.anchor: قال: «فما جعلكم أطول الناس أعمارا؟» . قالوا: من قبل أنا نتعاطى الحق، ونحكم بالعدل.

rows.speaker: القوم
rows.claim: They avoid sorrow and anger because they prepared themselves for hardship from the beginning and welcomed it.
rows.anchor: قال: «فما بالكم لا تحزنون ولا تحردون؟» . قالوا: من قبل أنا وطنا أنفسنا للبلاء مذ كنا،

rows.speaker: القوم
rows.claim: They escape the usual afflictions by relying on God alone and not practicing astrological weather divination.
rows.anchor: قال: «فما بالكم لا يصيبكم الآفات كما يصيب الناس؟» . قالوا: لأنا لا نتوكل على غير الله،

rows.speaker: القوم
rows.claim: They inherited from their ancestors mercy to the needy, pardoning and kindness, patience, kinship, trustworthiness, timely prayer, fulfilled pledges, and truthful promises; God rectified and protected them and their descendants.
rows.anchor: وجدنا آباءنا يرحمون مساكينهم، ويواسون فقراءهم، ويعفون عمن ظلمهم، ويحسنون إلى من أساء إليهم،

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra says Gog and Magog dig at the barrier daily; God restores it until their appointed release, when they emerge, drink waters, hide people in forts, and shoot arrows that return bloodied, before worms kill them and beasts fatten on their flesh.
rows.anchor: وروى قتادة عن أبي رافع عن أبي هريرة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «إن يأجوج ومأجوج يحفرونه كل يوم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report from Abu Saeed says Gog and Magog emerge in waves; the first drink the Tigris dry, later people remember it once held water, and they claim victory over earth before their arrows return bloodied from the sky.
rows.anchor: وروى محمود بن قتادة عن أبي سعيد الخدري أنه قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: «يفتح يأجوج ومأجوج

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: God sends a worm-like plague that kills them; Muslims find them dead, then their livestock grow lush on their flesh like plants after rain.
rows.anchor: هم كذلك إذ يبعث الله عز وجل عليهم دودا كنغف الجراد فيموتون موت الجراد،

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb says they drink the sea, eat its creatures, then wood, trees, and people, but cannot reach Mecca, Medina, or Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: قال وهب: إنهم كانوا يأتون البحر فيشربون ماءها، ويأكلون دوابها،

rows.speaker: قراء أهل الكوفة
rows.claim: The Kufans read kharājan with an alif while the others read kharjan; both forms mean payment, though Abu Amr distinguishes a voluntary gift from an obligatory levy.
rows.anchor: في قوله تعالى: فهل نجعل لك خرجا قرأ أهل الكوفة: (خراجا) بالألف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people ask Dhu al-Qarnayn for payment to erect a barrier that will keep Gog and Magog from reaching them.
rows.anchor: على أن تجعل بيننا وبينهم سدا: حاجزا فلا يصلون إلينا؟

rows.speaker: قراء أهل مكة
rows.claim: Meccan readers pronounce makkannan with two nūns rather than the assimilated makkannī reading; Dhu al-Qarnayn says God's empowerment is better, yet asks them to assist with strength.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أهل مكة: (ما مكنني) بنونين بالإظهار

rows.speaker: ذو القرنين
rows.claim: He proposes a barrier like a wall or dam and asks the people to help with physical strength.
rows.anchor: ولكن أعينوني بقوة أجعل بينكم وبينهم ردما: حاجزا كالحائط والسد.

rows.speaker: ذو القرنين
rows.claim: He explains that the required help is skilled builders and craftsmen who know construction and tools.
rows.anchor: قالوا: وما تلك القوة؟ قال: «فعلة وصناع يحسنون البناء والعمل والآلة»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He requests iron blocks, builds up to the level of the two mountain slopes, and alternates timber and iron; one report says he burns the timber and pours molten copper so it replaces the wood and binds to iron.
rows.anchor: قال: آتوني زبر الحديد يعني: أعطوني قطع الحديد، واحدتها زبرة، فأتوه بها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two ṣadafayn are the mountains; their noun is read with either both consonants rounded or both opened, and qiṭr means molten copper poured over the heated structure.
rows.anchor: وهما الجبلان- بضم الصاد والدال، وفتحهما- وأمر بالنار فأرسلت فيه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people can neither climb over the barrier nor bore through it from below.
rows.anchor: فما اسطاعوا أن يظهروه ويعلوه من فوقه، وما استطاعوا له نقبا من أسفله.

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Qatada says a man told the Prophet he had seen the barrier, describing it as brocade with alternating black and red stripes; the Prophet affirmed it.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة ذكر لنا أن رجلا قال: يا نبي الله قد رأيت سد يأجوج ومأجوج.

rows.speaker: ذو القرنين
rows.claim: Dhu al-Qarnayn calls the barrier a mercy from God, hence the feminine demonstrative is not used.
rows.anchor: هذا السد رحمة: نعمة من ربي فلذلك لم يقل: هذه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God's promise comes, the barrier will be flattened level with the ground; dakka without length means crushed, while dakkaʾ evokes a flat-backed camel.
rows.anchor: فإذا جاء وعد ربي جعله دكاء ملتزقة مستوية بالأرض من قولهم: ناقة دكاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the end, people intermingle in confusion, the trumpet is blown, all are gathered on one plain, and Hell is displayed to unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وتركنا بعضهم، يعني الخلق يومئذ يموج: يدخل في بعض ويختلط إنسهم بجنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers' eyes are veiled from God's remembrance, meaning faith and the Quran; they cannot bear to hear, reflect on, or believe the Book, either from deep misery or hostility to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: ثم وصفهم فقال: الذين كانت أعينهم في غطاء: غشاوة وغفلة عن ذكري، يعني:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afahasiba means he thought or supposed.
rows.anchor: أفحسب: أفظن.

rows.speaker: قراء عكرمة ومجاهد وعلي
rows.claim: These readers give afahasbu as meaning whether that is enough for them.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة ومجاهد وعلي: (أفحسب) ، أي كفاهم ذلك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the servants taken as allies as devils whom people follow and obey instead of God.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يعني: الشياطين، تولوهم وأطاعوهم من دون الله.

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil identifies the supposed allies as idols, called servants as in 7:194.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: يعني: الأصنام، وسماهم عبادا كما قال في موضع آخر:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression presents Hell as lodging prepared for the unbelievers.
rows.anchor: إنا أعتدنا جهنم للكافرين نزلا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greatest losers are people who tire themselves in work hoping for profit but end in ruin, like a merchant whose investment fails.
rows.anchor: يعني الذين أتعبوا أنفسهم في عمل يبتغون به ربحا، فنالوا به هلاكا وعطبا،

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says Paradise has one hundred levels separated by the distance between heaven and earth; Firdaws is highest, its rivers flow from it, and the Throne is above it, so believers should ask for Firdaws.
rows.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «الجنة مائة درجة، ما بين كل درجتين كما بين السماء والأرض.

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report from Abu Musa describes four Firdaws gardens, two built and furnished with gold and two with silver; only the veil of divine majesty prevents the people from seeing their Lord.
rows.anchor: قال: «جنات الفردوس أربع: جنتان من ذهب أبنيتهما وما فيهما، وجنتان من فضة

rows.speaker: شهر
rows.claim: Shahr says God created the Garden of Firdaws with His hand and opens it each Thursday, telling it to increase in beauty and fragrance for His friends.
rows.anchor: وقال شهر: خلق الله جنة الفردوس بيده فهو يفتحها في كل يوم خميس فيقول: ازدادي حسنا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada calls Firdaws the elevated central and best part of Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: الفردوس ربوة الجنة وأوسطها وأفضلها وأرفعها.

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة
rows.claim: Abu Umama calls Firdaws the center of Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو أمامة: الفردوس سرة الجنة.

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb says no garden is above Firdaws and that it contains those who enjoin right and forbid wrong.
rows.anchor: وقال كعب: ليس في الجنان جنة أعلى من جنة الفردوس وفيها الآمرون بالمعروف

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses Firdaws as a garden in the Roman language.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: هو البستان بالرومية.

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb also glosses Firdaws as a garden containing grapevines.
rows.anchor: وقال كعب: هو البستان فيه الأعناب.

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak describes it as a Paradise with dense trees.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: هي الجنة الملتفة الأشجار.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view calls Firdaws a beautiful meadow; another calls it valleys where many kinds of plants grow, with farādis as its plural, attested by Umayya's poetry.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هي الروضة المستحسنة. وقيل: هي الأودية التي تنبت ضروبا من النبات، وجمعها فراديس:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of Paradise never seek to move away; ḥawlan means relocation and is a verbal noun like ṣaʿar and ʿiwaj.
rows.anchor: خالدين فيها لا يبغون عنها حولا أي يطلبون عنها تحولا إلى غيرها، وهو مصدر مثل الصعر والعوج.

rows.speaker: بعض أصحاب أنس
rows.claim: Mukhallad ibn al-Husayn heard that the first entrant thinks he was admitted first because no one is better, while the last thinks none received a gift like his.
rows.anchor: قال مخلد بن الحسين: سمعت بعض أصحاب أنس قال: يقول أولهم دخولا: إنما أدخلني الله أولهم لأنه ليس أحد أفضل مني.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Jews challenged the Prophet: how can they have been given great wisdom while revelation says human knowledge is little? The response is that the ocean would run out before God's words, wisdom, and wonders.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: قالت اليهود: يا محمد تزعم أنا قد أوتينا الحكمة، وفي كتابك: ومن يؤت الحكمة فقد أوتي خيرا كثيرا

rows.speaker: قراء أهل الكوفة
rows.claim: The Kufans read yanfuḏ with yāʾ in before it runs out, matching the preceding verb; Ubayy's codex reads madādan, compared with 31:27.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أهل الكوفة (قبل أن ينفد) بالياء لتقدم الفعل، ولو جئنا بمثله مددا:

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed about Jundub ibn Zuhayr al-Amiri, who was pleased when others saw his worship; the Prophet taught that God accepts only pure deeds not shared with another.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: نزلت في جندب بن زهير العامري، وذلك أنه

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports that a man loved fighting for God and also wanted people to see his valor; this verse was revealed about the case.
rows.anchor: وقال أنس: قال رجل: يا نبي الله، إني أحب الجهاد في سبيل الله، وأحب أن يرى مكاني،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to state that he is an ordinary human, created as other people are.
rows.anchor: قل يا محمد: إنما أنا بشر مثلكم: خلق آدمي مثلكم.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: God taught the Messenger humility so that he would not grow proud before creation.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: علم الله رسوله التواضع لئلا يزهو على خلقه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hoping to meet the Lord means reaching Him, or hoping to see Him; hope encompasses both fear and expectation, as illustrated by a poet's line.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه يأمل رؤية ربه، فالرجاء يتضمن معنيين: الخوف والأمل،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Righteous action must be sincere, and worship must not be shared with anyone, which means avoiding ostentation.
rows.anchor: فليعمل عملا صالحا: خالصا ولا يشرك بعبادة ربه أحدا، أي ولا يراء.

rows.speaker: شهر بن حوشب
rows.claim: A man asks Ubadah ibn al-Samit about worship done for God while also seeking praise; Ubadah says it earns nothing because God rejects any deed shared with a partner.
rows.anchor: قال شهر ابن حوشب: جاء رجل إلى عبادة بن الصامت، فقال: أرأيت رجلا يصلي

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra begins a report in which the Prophet warns against minor associationism; the excerpt ends before the companions' question is answered.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «اتقوا الشرك الأصغر»

rows.speaker: قراء أبي عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr reads the hāʾ with kasra and yāʾ with fatḥa in the disjoint letters; Shammi, Hamza, and Khalaf use two kasras, Kisai two fatḥas, and Ibn Kathir, Asim, and Yaqub are also listed in the reading discussion.
rows.anchor: قوله عز وجل كهيعص قرأ أبو عمرو بكسر الهاء وفتح الياء، ضده شامي وحمزة وخلف، بكسرهما،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the letters are one of God's names; another view calls them the greatest name.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: هو اسم من أسماء الله عز وجل، وقيل: إنه اسم الله الأعظم،

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the letters are a name for the Quran.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: هو اسم من اسماء القرآن،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says the letters name the surah.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو اسم السورة،

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب وابن عباس
rows.claim: Ali and Ibn Abbas say the letters are an oath by which God swears.
rows.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب وابن عباس: هو قسم أقسم الله تعالى به

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says they are praise by which God praises Himself.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: هو ثناء أثنى الله عز وجل به [على] نفسه.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas assigns the letters meanings: K for Generous, H for Guide, Y for Merciful, Ayn for Knowing and Great, and Sad for Truthful.
rows.anchor: قال: الكاف من كريم، والهاء من هاد، والياء من رحيم والعين من عليم وعظيم، والصاد من صادق،

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi also expands the letters as God's sufficiency for creation, guidance for servants, hand above their hands, knowledge of creation, and truth of promise.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي أيضا: معناه: كاف لخلقه، هاد لعباده، يده فوق أيديهم، عالم ببريته، صادق في وعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The syntax may take the letters as nominative, or read the phrase with fronting and postponement: the Lord mentions Zachariah with mercy, with Zachariah in the accusative.
rows.anchor: ذكر رفع ب كهيعص وإن شئت قلت: هذا ذكر رحمت ربك عبده زكريا، وفيه تقديم وتأخير،

rows.speaker: قراء بعضهم
rows.claim: Some read ʿabdahu Zakariyya with Zakariyya in the nominative, making him the subject of the verb.
rows.anchor: وقرأ بعضهم عبده زكريا بالرفع على أن الفعل له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zachariah prayed secretly in his sanctuary at night, where offerings were brought near, sincerely and unseen by anyone but God.
rows.anchor: إذ نادى دعا ربه في محرابه حيث يقرب القربان نداء خفيا دعاء سرا من قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His bones had weakened, his head had turned gray, and he had grown old and weak, nearing death.
rows.anchor: قال رب إني وهن ضعف العظم مني واشتعل الرأس شيبا شمطا، يقول:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says he had never been disappointed in prayer because God had made a habit of answering him.
rows.anchor: ولم أكن بدعائك رب شقيا يقول: يا رب عودتني الإجابة فيما كنت تجيبني إذا دعوتك

rows.speaker: قراء عثمان ويحيى بن يعمر
rows.claim: They read khift with an open khāʾ and doubled fāʾ, meaning the heirs had dwindled and become few.
rows.anchor: قرأ عثمان ويحيى بن يعمر، (خفت) بفتح الخاء والفاء وكسر التاء مشددا الموالي بسكون الياء

rows.speaker: قراء الباقون
rows.claim: The other readers take khift as fear and al-mawālī as its accusative object: Zachariah fears an heir other than a son.
rows.anchor: الباقون: (خفت) بكسر الخاء وضم التاء من الخوف، الموالي نصبا، خاف أن يرثه غير الولد،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says he feared his heirs would alter God's religion and rulings, and asked for a righteous child to safeguard his community.
rows.anchor: وقيل: خاف عليهم تبديل دين الله عز وجل وتغيير أحكامه وأن لا يحسنوا الخلافة له على أمته،

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses mawālī as the clan or agnatic relatives.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: العصبة،

rows.speaker: أبو صالح
rows.claim: Abu Salih glosses mawālī as the kalālah, collateral heirs.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو صالح: الكلالة،

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi glosses mawālī as the heirs who remain after his death.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: الورثة من ورائي من بعد موتي

rows.speaker: قراء يحيى بن يعمر ويحيى بن وثاب والأعمش وأبي عمرو والكسائي
rows.claim: These readers put both inheritance verbs in the jussive as the response to a supplication; the others use nominatives as a circumstantial or descriptive clause, meaning an inheriting child.
rows.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن يعمر ويحيى بن وثاب والأعمش وأبو عمرو والكسائي بالجزم فيهما على جواب الدعاء،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ويحيى بن يعمر
rows.claim: They understand inheritance from Zachariah and Jacob's family as inheritance of prophethood and knowledge.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس ويحيى بن يعمر: يرثني، وأرث من آل يعقوب النبوة،

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says the child inherits Zachariah's wealth and the prophethood and priestly office of Jacob's family.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: معناه يرثني مالي ويرث من آل يعقوب النبوة والحبورة،

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi identifies this Jacob as Matan's son and Zachariah's brother, not Joseph's father.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: هو يعقوب بن ماثان أخو زكريا وليس يعقوب أب يوسف

rows.speaker: أبو صالح
rows.claim: Abu Salih interprets the request to make the child pleasing as a request to make him a prophet like his father.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو صالح: معناه: اجعله نبيا كما جعلت أباه نبيا.

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report from Qatada through Bishr ibn Nahik says the Prophet prayed for mercy on Zachariah, who had no need of heirs.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة عن بشر بن نهيك أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا قرأ هذه الآية يرثني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The announcement condenses the response to Zachariah's prayer: God promises a boy named Yahya.
rows.anchor: فيه إضمار واختصار، يعني فاستجاب دعاءه فقال: يا زكريا إنا نبشرك بغلام

rows.speaker: قتادة والكلبي
rows.claim: Qatada and al-Kalbi, with Ikrima's report from Ibn Abbas, say no one before Yahya bore that name.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة والكلبي: لم يسم أحد قبله يحيى، وهي رواية عكرمة عن ابن عباس،

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وعطاء
rows.claim: Saeed ibn Jubayr and Ata interpret samiyyan as having no equal, as in 19:65; Mujahid transmits this from Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير وعطاء: لم نجعل له شبيها، ومثله دليله قوله تعالى هل تعلم له سميا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this view, Yahya had no equal because he never intended disobedience; one view also makes him unmatched among women because he was a master and celibate.
rows.anchor: وتأويل هذا القول أنه لم يكن له مثل لأنه لم يهم بمعصيته قط وقيل:

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ali reports Ibn Abbas's view that barren women had never borne a child like Yahya.
rows.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب عن ابن عباس: لم تلد العواقر مثله ولدا،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One interpretation says God qualified the claim with before because He intended to create someone greater afterward, Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن الله تعالى اشترط القبل لأنه جل ذكره أراد أن يخلق بعده من هو أفضل منه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other views limit the statement to some qualities, since it need not grant Yahya superiority in every respect and earlier patriarchs were greater.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن الله تعالى لم يرد بهذا القول جميع الفضائل كلها ليحيى،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question how he could have a boy uses kāna with an adjectival predicate, like the question about a child in the cradle.
rows.anchor: وكانت امرأتي عاقرا أي وامرأتي عاقر كقوله كيف نكلم من كان في المهد صبيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAtiyyan means dryness; Qatada explains it as the bones becoming desiccated, while ʿātin can describe a hardhearted or extremely wicked person.
rows.anchor: وقد بلغت من الكبر عتيا أي يبسا، قال قتادة: نحول العظم

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd says ʿatā and ʿasā describe anyone extreme in evil or disbelief.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيد: هو كل مبالغ في شر أو كفر فقد عتا وعسا،

rows.speaker: أبي وابن عباس
rows.claim: Ubayy and Ibn Abbas read ʿasiyyan; Yahya ibn Wathab, Hamza, and Kisai use a kasra in ʿatiyyan, while the others use a damma, both being dialect forms.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي وابن عباس عسيا، وقرأ يحيى بن وثاب وحمزة والكسائي عتيا بكسر العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God reminds Zachariah that He created him before, when he was nothing, so bringing him a child is easy.
rows.anchor: وقد خلقتك من قبل، من قبل يحيى، ولم تك شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zachariah asks for a sign of his wife's pregnancy; his sign is inability to speak to people for three nights while otherwise healthy and sound.
rows.anchor: قال رب اجعل لي آية على حمل امرأتي قال آيتك ألا تكلم الناس ثلاث ليال سويا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People waited behind the sanctuary to enter and pray; Zachariah emerged changed in appearance and communicated by gesture or by writing on the ground, directing them to pray at dawn and dusk.
rows.anchor: وكان الناس من وراء المحراب ينتظرونه أن يفتح لهم الباب فيدخلون ويصلون إذ خرج عليهم زكريا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yahya is told to take the Scripture earnestly and was given understanding as a child.
rows.anchor: قوله يا يحيى خذ الكتاب بقوة بجد وآتيناه الحكم يعني الفهم صبيا

rows.speaker: معمر
rows.claim: Maʿmar recounts that when children invited Yahya to play, he answered that he was not created for play; this illustrates wisdom in childhood.
rows.anchor: وقال معمر: جاء صبيان إلى يحيى بن زكريا فقالوا: اخرج بنا نلعب، فقال: ما للعب خلقت،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥanān means mercy or compassion, supported by lines from al-Hutayʾa and Tarafa; the word derives from a mother's longing for her calf.
rows.anchor: وحنانا من لدنا رحمة من عندنا، قال الحطيئة لعمر بن الخطاب:

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says he does not know hanān except as God's tender mercy toward His servants.
rows.anchor: قال: ما أدري ما حنانا إلا أن يكون بعطف رحمة الله عز وجل على عباده

rows.speaker: عوف
rows.claim: Awf says he heard hanān explained as love.
rows.anchor: عن عوف بلغني في قوله الله عز وجل وحنانا من لدنا قال: الحنان: المحبة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses zakāh as obedience to God and sincerity.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس يعني بالزكاة طاعة الله عز وجل والإخلاص.

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says zakāh is righteous, pure action.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: هي الفعل الزاكي الصالح،

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says zakāh means charity Yahya's father gave to his parents.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: يعني صدقة تصدق والده بها على أبويه،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other glosses take zakāh as blessing and increase, or as God's making Yahya pure from sins.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بركة ونماء وزيادة. وقيل: جعلناه طاهرا من الذنوب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yahya was a Muslim, sincere, and obedient servant.
rows.anchor: وكان تقيا مسلما مخلصا مطيعا.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: A report from Hasan attributes to the Prophet that everyone has contemplated or committed a sin except Yahya ibn Zachariah.
rows.anchor: قال: سمعت الحسن قال: إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «والذي نفسي بيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yahya was dutiful to both parents and did not disobey them.
rows.anchor: وبرا بوالديه بارا بهما لا يعصيهما

rows.speaker: الحلبي
rows.claim: Al-Halabi explains jabbār as an arrogant person; he also glosses it as one who beats and kills in anger.
rows.anchor: قال الحلبي: الجبار الذي يضرب ويقتل على الغضب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAṣiyyan means strongly disobedient to his Lord.
rows.anchor: عصيا شديد العصيان لربه.

rows.speaker: الحلبي
rows.claim: Al-Halabi says the peace is from God for Yahya at birth, death, and resurrection.
rows.anchor: وسلام عليه قال الحلبي: سلام له منا حين ولد وحين يموت وحين يبعث حيا.

rows.speaker: الحسن عن قتادة
rows.claim: Hasan reports that Jesus and Yahya each asked the other to seek forgiveness, each calling the other better; Jesus said he had blessed himself while God blessed Yahya.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة عن الحسن أن يحيى وعيسى عليهما السلام التقيا فقال له عيسى: استغفر لي فأنت خير مني،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary is identified as the daughter of Imran ibn Mathan; she withdrew from her family to a place toward the east, in a part of the home used during winter.
rows.anchor: وهي ابنة عمران بن ماثان إذ انتبذت.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada glosses intibādh as separating herself from others.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: انفردت.

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi glosses it as moving aside, deriving the word from something cast away.
rows.anchor: الكلبي: تنحت وأصله من النبذة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hasan says Christians adopted the east as their prayer direction because Mary withdrew to an eastern place.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: اتخذت النصارى المشرق قبلة لأن مريم انتبذت مكانا شرقيا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Mary's ḥijāb was a screen; Muqatil says she placed a mountain between herself and her people.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: سترا، قال مقاتل: جعلت الجبل بينها وبين قومها،

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says Mary stayed in the mosque when pure and went to her aunt's house during menstruation; while washing, she encountered Gabriel as a handsome, smooth-faced young man.
rows.anchor: قال عكرمة: إن مريم كانت تكون في المسجد ما دامت طاهرا، فإذا حاضت تحولت إلى بيت خالتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spirit sent to Mary is Gabriel, or the spirit of Jesus by an honorific attribution.
rows.anchor: فذلك قوله فأرسلنا إليها روحنا يعني جبرئيل (عليه السلام) وقيل: روح عيسى ابن مريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel appeared fully human so Mary could remain composed and hear him; his true form would have frightened her and prevented her from listening.
rows.anchor: لم ينقص منه شيء وإنما أرسله في صورة البشر لتثبت مريم عليها السلام وتقدر على استماع كلامه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary's taqiyyan means a believer who is obedient.
rows.anchor: قالت إني أعوذ بالرحمن منك إن كنت تقيا مؤمنا مطيعا.

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali says Mary knew a pious person exercises restraint.
rows.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طالب: علمت أن التقي ذو نهية

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account says Taqi was one of the most upright people of the time, and Mary invoked refuge if Gabriel was as upright as he.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كان تقي رجل من أعدل الناس في ذلك الزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage stresses that an unrelated man and woman were alone in a private place; Gabriel says he is God's messenger, meaning that he announces God's gift of a pure son.
rows.anchor: كيف يكون رجل اجنبي وامرأة اجنبية في حجاب واحد؟ قال لها جبرئيل إنما أنا رسول ربك لأهب لك

rows.speaker: قراء أبي عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr reads li-yahaba in the third person, meaning he will give, instead of the first-person reading.
rows.anchor: أي يقول لأهب لك، وقرأ أبو عمرو ليهب بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakiyyan means a righteous, pious boy.
rows.anchor: ولدا غلاما زكيا صالحا تقيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary says no man has touched her and she has not been a prostitute; the feminine ending is omitted because the word departs from its expected form.
rows.anchor: قالت مريم أنى يكون لي غلام ولم يمسسني بشر ولم يقربني روح ولم أك بغيا فاجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel confirms God's decree: creating a child without a father is easy, and Jesus will be a sign to people and a mercy to those who follow his religion.
rows.anchor: وقيل هكذا قال ربك هو علي هين خلق ولد من غير أب ولنجعله آية علامة هذه للناس ورحمة منا لمن تبعه على دينه.

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says Mary's cousin Yusuf heard she was pregnant through adultery and that the king meant to kill her; he fled with her, then Gabriel stopped him from killing her by explaining she bore the Holy Spirit.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: قيل لابن عم لها يقال له يوسف: إن مريم حملت من الزنا لأن يقتلها الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reported duration of Mary's pregnancy varies: nine months, eight months with Jesus uniquely surviving an eight-month birth, six months, three hours, or one hour.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا في مدة حملها ووقت وضعها، فقال بعضهم: كان مقدار حملها تسعة أشهر كحمل سائر النساء،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says she conceived and gave birth immediately, with only an hour between pregnancy and withdrawing, since the Quran names no interval.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ما هو إلا أن حملت فوضعت ولم يكن بين الحمل والانتباذ إلا ساعة:

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن سليمان
rows.claim: Muqatil says Mary conceived, the child formed, and she gave birth in successive hours at noon; she was ten and had menstruated twice before conceiving.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل بن سليمان: حملته مريم في ساعة وصور في ساعة ووضعته في ساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ajāʾahā means labor compelled and brought her; Abdullah's reading āwāhā means labor sheltered her, and the term may mean pregnancy or contractions.
rows.anchor: فأجاءها المخاض ألجأها وجاء بها المخاض، وفي قراءة عبد الله آواها المخاض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The palm trunk was dry, leafless, and in the desert during severe winter; one report says it was a dry trunk brought to build Bethlehem.
rows.anchor: إلى جذع النخلة وكانت نخلة يابسة في الصحراء في شدة الشتاء ولم يكن لها سعف.

rows.speaker: قراء يحيى بن وثاب والأعمش وحمزة
rows.claim: These readers pronounce nasyan with an open nūn; the others use a kasra, and both forms are dialects meaning something forgotten.
rows.anchor: قالت يا ليتني مت قبل هذا وكنت نسيا منسيا قرأ يحيى بن وثاب والأعمش وحمزة: نسيا بفتح النون،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses nasyan as something left behind and abandoned.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يعني شيئا متروكا،

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada glosses it as something no one remembers or knows.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: شيئا لا يذكر ولا يعرف،

rows.speaker: عكرمة والضحاك ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ikrima, al-Dahhak, and Mujahid interpret nasyan as a discarded menstrual clot.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة والضحاك ومجاهد: حيضة ملقاة.

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: Al-Rabiʿ interprets it as a miscarriage.
rows.anchor: قال الربيع: هو السقط

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says it means something destroyed or perished.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: يعني كالشيء الهالك.

rows.speaker: عطاء بن أبي مسلم
rows.claim: Ata ibn Abi Muslim says it means that she had never been created.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء بن أبي مسلم: يعني لم أخلق،

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ explains the word as the menstrual cloth a woman throws away.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: هو ما تلقيه المرأة من خرق اعتلالها،

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd says nasyan is something trivial that was forgotten or neglected.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيد: هو ما نسي وأغفل من شيء حقير.
